overview: The 2021 Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act set aside money for the Interior Department to repair or replace certain aging dams in the West. This bill lets some of that money also go to dams built under the Carey Act, an 1894 law that encouraged private irrigation projects on federal land in Western states, as long as those dams are still operating. The Interior Secretary could fund these Carey Act dam projects only after deciding that the dams already eligible under the 2021 law have received the money they need and that funds are still left over. The bill affects farmers and communities that rely on these older irrigation dams. As of September 17, 2026, a Senate committee had approved it and it was placed on the Senate calendar for possible floor action.
for: Supporters say many century-old Carey Act dams need repairs for safety and reliable irrigation, and this lets leftover infrastructure money help them without new spending or taking funds from projects already in line.
against: Critics say it widens a program meant for federal water projects to include privately developed dams, which could stretch limited repair money further and benefit private irrigation owners.
